name: S-Class: Warpriest
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced.

The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

Warpriest, S-Class

S-class warpriests serve their deities as champions with a heavier hand than a cleric and a more magical approach to their faith than a paladin. Sacred weapon in hand, these s-class warpriests trek into battle, ready to get into their opponents’ faces and go toe-to-toe.

Role: S-class warpriests maintain their original role as healers and protectors, but that role is expanded with more access to spells through full domains and the ability to cast their domain spells using any warpriest spell slot.

Note: With one small exception, the s-class warpriest is an alternate, superior version of the warpriest class. They retain all of the standard warpriest progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select warpriest archetypes without specific adjustments. Archetypes that modify or replace an s-class warpriest’s major blessings at 10th level do so at 9th level instead.

Alignment: An s-class warpriest’s alignment must be within one step of their deity’s, along either the law/chaos axis or the good/evil axis.

Hit Die: d8.

Parent Classes: Cleric and fighter.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, an s-class warpriest begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class warpriest’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class warpriest.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

S-class warpriests are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, as well as the favored weapon of their deity, and with all armor (heavy, light, and medium) and shields (except tower shields). If the s-class warpriest worships a deity with unarmed strike as its favored weapon, the s-class warpriest gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat.

Spellcasting

An s-class warpriest casts divine spells which are drawn from the warpriest spell list. Their alignment, however, may restrict them from casting certain spells opposed to their moral or ethical beliefs; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful spells. An s-class warpriest must choose and prepare their spells in advance.

To prepare or cast a spell, an s-class warpriest must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level.

The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against an s-class warpriest’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the s-class warpriest’s Wisdom modifier.

Like other spellcasters, an s-class warpriest can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Warpriest. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they has a high Wisdom score.

S-class warpriests meditate or pray for their spells. Each warpriest must choose a time at which they must spend 1 hour each day in quiet contemplation or supplication to regain their daily allotment of spells. Time spent resting has no effect on whether an s-class warpriest can prepare spells. An s-class warpriest may prepare and cast any spell on the warpriest spell list, provided that they can cast spells of that level, but they must choose which spells to prepare during their daily meditation.

Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells: An s-class warpriest can’t cast spells of an alignment opposed to their own or their deity’s (if they have one). Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaotic, evil, good, and lawful descriptors in their spell descriptions.

Orisons: S-class warpriests can prepare a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on Table: S-Class Warpriest under “Spells per day.” These spells are treated like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.

Domains

An s-class warpriest’s deity influences their alignment, what magic they can perform, their values, and how others see them. An s-class warpriest chooses three domains from among those belonging to their deity. An s-class warpriest can select an alignment domain (Chaos, Evil, Good, or Law) only if their alignment matches that domain. If an s-class warpriest is not devoted to a particular deity, they still select three domains to represent their spiritual inclinations and abilities (subject to GM approval). The restriction on alignment domains still applies. Three sample domains can be found at the end of this section.

Domain Powers: Each domain grants a number of domain powers, dependent upon the level of the s-class warpriest, as well as a number of bonus spells. At the beginning of each day, an s-class warpriest selects two of the domain powers granted by their domains. They must be high enough level to select those powers. They can select additional domain powers at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. At 17th level, the s-class warpriest should have access to all of the powers granted by each of their three domains. Unless otherwise noted, activating a domain power is a standard action.

Blessings: If a domain also grants warpriest blessings, an s-class warpriest can select those blessings as domain powers when they choose their powers each morning. They can call upon the power of their blessings a number of times per day (in any combination) equal to 3 + 1/2 their warpriest level (to a maximum of 13 times per day at 20th level).

Domain Spells: In addition to their spells per day, an s-class warpriest gains access to their domains’ 1stthrough 6th-level spells, which they can prepare using their warpriest spell slots. The s-class warpriest adds those spells to their warpriest spell list, and they must prepare at least one of each spell level they can cast each day.

Sacred Weapon (Su)

At 1st level, weapons wielded by an s-class warpriest are charged with the power of their faith. In addition to the favored weapon of their deity, the s-class warpriest can designate a weapon as a sacred weapon by selecting that weapon with the Weapon Focus feat; if they have multiple Weapon Focus feats, this ability applies to all of them. Whenever the s-class warpriest hits with their sacred weapon, the weapon damage is based on their level and not the weapon type.

Level Range	Size
Small	Medium	Large
1st-4th	1d4	1d6	1d8
5th-9th	1d6	1d8	2d6
10th-14th	1d8	1d10	2d8
15th-19th	1d10	2d6	3d6
20th	2d6	2d8	3d8

The s-class warpriest can decide to use the weapon’s base damage instead of the sacred weapon damage—this must be declared before the attack roll is made. (If the weapon’s base damage exceeds the sacred weapon damage, its damage is unchanged.) This increase in damage does not affect any other aspect of the weapon, and doesn’t apply to alchemical items, bombs, or other weapons that only deal energy damage.

At 4th level, the s-class warpriest gains the ability to enhance one of their sacred weapons with divine power as a swift action.

This power grants the weapon a +1 enhancement bonus.

For every 4 levels beyond 4th, this bonus increases by 1 (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level). If the s-class warpriest has more than one sacred weapon, they can enhance another on the following round by using another swift action. The s-class warpriest can use this ability a number of rounds per day equal to their warpriest level, but these rounds need not be consecutive.

If multiple weapons are enhanced, each one consumes rounds of use individually. The enhancement bonus and special abilities are determined the first time the ability is used each day, and cannot be changed until the next day.

These bonuses stack with any existing bonuses the weapon might have, to a maximum of +5. The s-class warpriest can enhance a weapon with any of the following weapon special abilities:

Alignment Weapon Special Abilities
Alignment	Abilities
Any	brilliant energy, defending, disruption, flaming, frost, keen, shock
Chaotic	anarchic, vicious
Evil	mighty cleaving, unholy
Good	ghost touch, holy
Lawful	axiomatic, merciful
Neutral	spell storing, thundering

Adding any of these special abilities replaces an amount of bonus equal to the special ability’s base cost. Duplicate abilities do not stack. The weapon must have at least a +1 enhancement bonus before any other special abilities can be added.

These bonuses do not apply if another creature is wielding the weapon, but they continue to be in effect if the weapon otherwise leaves the s-class warpriest’s possession (such as if the weapon is thrown). This ability can be ended as a free action at the start of the s-class warpriest’s turn (that round does not count against the total duration, unless the ability is resumed during the same round). If the s-class warpriest uses this ability on a double weapon, the effects apply to only one end of the weapon.

Spontaneous Casting

A good s-class warpriest (or a neutral s-class warpriest of a good deity) can channel stored spell energy into healing spells that they did not prepare ahead of time. The s-class warpriest can “lose” any prepared spell that is not an orison or domain spell in order to cast any cure spell of the same spell level or lower (a cure spell is any spell with “cure” in its name).

An evil s-class warpriest (or a neutral s-class warpriest of an evil deity) can’t convert prepared spells to cure spells but can convert them to inflict spells (an inflict spell is one with “inflict” in its name).

An s-class warpriest who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can convert spells to either cure spells or inflict spells (player’s choice). Once the player makes this choice, it cannot be reversed. This choice also determines whether the s-class warpriest channels positive or negative energy (see channel energy).

Warpriest Tactics (Ex)

At 1st level, an s-class warpriest receives Weapon Focus as a bonus feat (they can choose any weapon, not just their deity’s favored weapon).

At 5th level, the s-class warpriest also receive Selective Channeling.

Bonus Languages

An s-class warpriest’s bonus language options include Abyssal, Celestial, and Infernal. These choices are in addition to the bonus languages available to the character because of their race.

Fervor (Su)

At 2nd level, an s-class warpriest can draw upon the power of their faith to heal wounds or harm foes. They can also use this ability to quickly cast spells that aid in their struggles. This ability can be used a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their warpriest level + their Wisdom modifier

Using this ability is a standard action (unless the s-class warpriest targets themselves, in which case it’s a swift action).

By expending one use of this ability, a good warpriest (or one who worships a good deity) can touch a creature to heal it of 1d6 points of damage, plus an additional 1d6 points of damage for every 3 warpriest levels they possesses above 2nd (to a maximum of 7d6 at 20th level). Alternatively, the s-class warpriest can use this ability to harm an undead creature, dealing the same amount of damage they would otherwise heal with a melee touch attack. Using fervor in this way is a standard action that provokes an attack of opportunity.

Undead do not receive a saving throw against this damage. This counts as positive energy.

An evil warpriest (or one who worships an evil deity) can use this ability to instead deal damage to living creatures with a melee touch attack and heal undead creatures with a touch. This counts as negative energy.

A neutral warpriest who worships a neutral deity (or one who is not devoted to a particular deity) uses this ability as a good warpriest if they chose to spontaneously cast cure spells or as an evil warpriest if they chose to spontaneously cast inflict spells.

As a swift action, an s-class warpriest can expend one use of this ability to cast any one warpriest spell they has prepared with a casting time of 1 round or shorter. When cast in this way, the spell can target only the s-class warpriest, even if it could normally affect other or multiple targets. Spells cast in this way ignore somatic components and do not provoke attacks of opportunity. The s-class warpriest does not need to have a free hand to cast a spell in this way.

Bonus Feats

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class warpriest gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats. The s-class warpriest must meet the prerequisites for these feats, but they treat their warpriest level as their base attack bonus (in addition to base attack bonuses gained from other classes and Hit Dice) for the purpose of qualifying for these feats.

Finally, for the purposes of these feats, the s-class warpriest can select feats that have a minimum number of fighter levels as a prerequisite, treating their warpriest level as their fighter level.

Channel Energy (Su)

Starting at 4th level, an s-class warpriest can release a wave of energy by channeling the power of their faith through their holy (or unholy) symbol. This energy can be used to deal or heal damage, depending on the type of energy channeled and the creatures targeted. Using this ability is a standard action that expends two uses of their fervor ability and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity.

The s-class warpriest must present a holy (or unholy) symbol to use this ability.

A good warpriest (or one who worships a good deity) channels positive energy and can choose to heal living creatures or to deal damage to undead creatures. An evil warpriest (or one who worships an evil deity) channels negative energy and can choose to deal damage to living creatures or heal undead creatures. A neutral warpriest who worships a neutral deity (or one who is not devoted to a particular deity) channels positive energy if they chose to spontaneously cast cure spells or negative energy if they chose to spontaneously cast inflict spells.

Channeling energy causes a burst that affects all creatures of one type (either undead or living) in a 30-foot radius centered on the s-class warpriest. The amount of damage dealt or healed is equal to the amount listed in the fervor ability. Creatures that take damage from channeled energy must succeed at a Will saving throw to halve the damage.

The save DC is 10 + 1/2 the s-class warpriest’s level + their Wisdom modifier

Creatures healed by channeled energy cannot exceed their maximum hit point total—all excess healing is lost.

An s-class warpriest can choose whether or not to include themselves in this effect.

Sacred Armor (Su)

At 7th level, the s-class warpriest gains the ability to enhance their armor with divine power as a swift action. This power grants the armor a +1 enhancement bonus. For every 3 levels beyond 7th, this bonus increases by 1 (to a maximum of +5 at 19th level). The s-class warpriest can use this ability a number of minutes per day equal to their warpriest level. This duration must be used in 1-minute increments, but they don’t need to be consecutive.

These bonuses stack with any existing bonuses the armor might have, to a maximum of +5. The s-class warpriest can enhance armor any of the following armor special abilities:

Alignment Weapon Special Abilities

Any energy resistance*, fortification*, glamered, spell resistance*

* This includes any higher versions of the special ability.

Adding any of these special abilities replaces an amount of bonus equal to the special ability’s base cost. For this purpose, glamered counts as a +1 bonus, energy resistance counts as +2, improved energy resistance counts as +4, and greater energy resistance counts as +5. Duplicate abilities do not stack. The armor must have at least a +1 enhancement bonus before any other special abilities can be added.

The enhancement bonus and armor special abilities are determined the first time the ability is used each day and cannot be changed until the next day. These bonuses apply only while the s-class warpriest is wearing the armor, and end immediately if the armor is removed or leaves the s-class warpriest’s possession. This ability can be ended as a free action at the start of the s-class warpriest’s turn. This ability cannot be applied to a shield.

When the s-class warpriest uses this ability, they can also use their sacred weapon ability as a free action by expending one use of their fervor.

Sacred Champion (Su)

At 20th level, the s-class warpriest becomes a true, mortal champion of their deity. Choose Aspect of War or Hammer of God. Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed:

Aspect of War: The s-class warpriest can channel an aspect of war, growing in power and martial ability. Once per day as a swift action, an s-class warpriest can treat their level as their base attack bonus, gains DR 10/—, and can move at their full speed regardless of the armor they are wearing or their encumbrance. In addition, the blessings they calls upon don’t count against their daily limit during this time. This ability lasts for 1 minute.

Greater Spontaneity: The s-class warpriest’s potential with divine magic overflows. They gain access to an expanded spell list. They choose 2 spells of each level they can cast (up to 6th) from the cleric’s spell list or their domains. The s-class warpriest no longer needs to prepare those spells. They can cast them spontaneously.

Hammer of God: The s-class warpriest has become one of their deity’s favorite weapons—the first tool that comes to hand when destruction is called for. The s-class warpriest can select two additional domain powers from any domains offered by their deity each morning. They can also call upon any blessings they choose two more times each day.

S-Class Warpriest Spell Suggestions

The following is a list of suggested spells for easy reference while playing an s-class warpriest. These spells are intentionally summarized here. If you would like to see the full rules for these spells, including at which levels other classes gain them, please refer to the individual resources.

0-Level: detect magic, detect poison, light, mending, read magic, resistance

1st-Level: cure light wounds, endure elements, obscuring mist, protection from law, resist energy, summon monster I

2nd-Level: align weapon, bear’s endurance, bull’s strength, cure moderate wounds, owl’s wisdom, protection from energy, summon monster II

3rd-Level: cure serious wounds, dispel magic, magic circle against law, scrying, summon monster III, water breathing

4th-Level: bull’s strength (mass), bear’s endurance (mass), chaos hammer, cure critical wounds, owl’s wisdom (mass), summon monster IV, true seeing

5th-Level: atonement, banishment, breath of life, cure light wounds (mass), dispel law, dispel magic (greater), ethereal jaunt, spell resistance, summon monster V

6th-Level: animate objects, cure moderate wounds (mass), dimensional lock, heal, scrying (greater), summon monster VI

S-Class Warpriest Blessings & Domains

These blessings and domains are available to both standard and s-class warpriests. Clerics can also select the domains here, granting them the powers and access to 7thlevel and higher domain spells.

Erosion
Rusting Touch (minor): You make a melee touch attack against a creature wearing metal armor or wielding a metal weapon. If you hit, choose a metal weapon, suit of metal armor, or metal shield carried or worn by that creature. The object takes an amount of hit point damage equal to 1d6 + half your warpriest level. If the item is not magical, or if your caster level is greater than the item’s caster level, this damage bypasses the item’s hardness.
Erosion Aura (major): At 10th level, you can project an aura of magically enhanced erosion as a standard action. Objects made primarily of metal or stone within this aura lose 10 points of hardness. Magic items retain a minimum hardness equal to twice their enhancement bonus and can attempt a Fortitude saving throw (DC = 10 + half your warpriest level + your Wisdom modifier) to negate this effect. A construct made primarily of metal or stone must succeed at a Fortitude save or lose all damage reduction and hardness for 1 round.
Ruins
Surefooted (minor): As a free action, your speed is not reduced by difficult terrain.
Remembrance (major): At 10th level, when within a ruin or other structure that is no longer claimed by civilization, you can call upon the wisdom of the land and its longdead residents. Once per day for every 4 warpriest levels you possess, you can cast divination as a spell-like ability. Additionally, if you are within ruins when you cast a divination spell, the spell’s range extends to the far edges of the ruins.
Sound
Bell Ringer (minor): At 1st level, you can cause your sacred weapon to vibrate with sound. This gives you a –5 circumstance penalty on Stealth checks, and allows your weapon to deal 1d4 additional sonic damage when you hit with it. This additional damage increases to 2d4 at 15th level.
Cacophonous Noise (major): At 10th level, when you create a sonic effect or cast a spell with an audible effect against an enemy, and that target fails its save (or Fortitude DC 10 + 1/2 your level + your Wisdom modifier if no save is present), it is deafened for a number of rounds equal to your Wisdom modifier.
Vermin
Familiar (minor): You gain a greensting scorpion familiar. Your effective wizard level for this ability is equal to your warpriest level. Your warpriest level stacks with levels from other classes that grant familiars when determining the powers of your familiar.
Vermin Friend (minor): You gain wild empathy as a druid of your warpriest level, but only to influence vermin.
Tremorsense (major): At 10th level, you gain tremorsense 30 feet. At 12th level, you gain tremorsense 60 feet.
Wealth
Wholesale (minor): You can purchase non-consumable items for half their total price. Once you purchase a number of items in this way equal to your Wisdom modifier, you must sell back one or more of those items before you can purchase more in this way.
Find What You Need (major): At 10th level, you can walk into a settlement with at least a 1% chance of finding a particular non-consumable item, find that item, and have enough to purchase it outright. The value of the item can be up to the listed amount at each level (wholesale does not work for this purchase), and you can only have one such item at a time. To purchase a new item with this ability, you must first sell back the one currently in your possession (you gain no actual currency in return, it simply fades and goes back to your deity once the transaction is complete).
